summary: Panguitch Municipal Airport (PNU) is a small general aviation facility serving the town of Panguitch in southern Utah, nestled in Garfield County at an elevation of approximately 6,600 feet. The airport primarily supports recreational flying and provides convenient access for visitors to nearby Bryce Canyon National Park, as well as other scenic destinations in the Grand Staircase–Escalante region. With its single runway and minimal infrastructure, PNU is favored by private pilots exploring the dramatic landscapes of the Colorado Plateau.
faqs:
Q: What is the main use of Panguitch Municipal Airport?
A: PNU serves primarily as a general aviation airport, supporting private and recreational flights rather than commercial airline service.

Q: Are there commercial flights to Panguitch?
A: No, the airport does not offer scheduled commercial flights. Travelers typically fly into larger regional airports and drive to Panguitch.

Q: What attractions are near the airport?
A: Bryce Canyon National Park is approximately 25 miles to the south, and several other scenic areas including Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument are within driving distance.

Q: What is the runway like at PNU?
A: The airport features a single asphalt runway suited for small general aviation aircraft, and pilots should be aware of the high-elevation terrain in the surrounding area.
transport_tips: Ground transportation is limited, so arranging a rental car or shuttle service in advance is recommended. The airport is located just a short drive from downtown Panguitch, with easy road access via US-89. Visitors flying in privately will find tie-down spaces and basic facilities but should plan to bring their own supplies.
local_tip: Contact the nearby Bryce Canyon Airport or local fixed-base operators ahead of time if you need fuel or transient services, as Panguitch Municipal has limited on-site amenities and services are not always available without prior arrangement.
